native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636 to -0.2293 (while becoming insignifcant) when both race and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: SES. The positive effect of socioeconomic status on BA degree completion is absorbed by academic preparation and race: in a logistic model with SES alone, a one-SD higher SES raises the odds of completing a bachelor's degree by ~42% (b=+0.3511, SE 0.0613, p=1.0e-08, OR 1.42), but once race and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite + high-school class percentile) are both included the SES coefficient reverses to -0.1720 (SE 0.0746, p=0.0211, OR 0.84) — a shift of -0.523 log-odds, i.e. 149% of the original effect, reducing the average marginal effect from +0.92 to -0.43 percentage points against a 2.69% base rate. SES is the only variable in the data showing this decrease from a positive baseline to a negative coefficient: ability (1.29->0.92), class percentile (1.15->0.56) and family size (-1.13->-1.05) retain sign and strong significance, and sex is never significant so cannot become insignificant. The attenuation is driven mainly by academic skill rather than race (adding academics alone already turns SES negative; adding race alone does not; dropping ASVAB from the full model restores SES to ~0), and collinearity is not responsible (VIF 1.33). The substantive claim is therefore attenuation/mediation-like: family SES affects bachelor's-degree attainment almost entirely through the academic skills and class rank it buys, leaving little or no residual direct SES effect. Stated honestly: under the agreed covariate definition the attenuated SES coefficient remains significant at alpha=0.05 (p=0.0211); the sign flip and the near-complete attenuation are robust across 720 sensitivity specifications, but the literal 'becomes insignificant' clause is reachable only by redefining academic characteristics to exclude ASVAB ability, which was not adopted.
native_result.WorkflowB: Inspection of data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8773 rows, 0 missing, bool outcome with 236 events/2.69%, raw continuous SES sd=0.742, text-label race/sex, only two academic columns). Estimator selection by scale calibration: LPM yields 0.01-0.03 (raw outcome) / 0.06-0.18 (z-outcome), so logistic regression on the log-odds scale was adopted as primary, with probit and OLS/LPM retained only in the sensitivity grid. Staged Wald logit models M0 candidate alone -> M1 +race -> M2 +academics -> M3 +race+academics (headline) -> M4 +sex/+family size (sensitivity); continuous predictors z-scored, race as two dummies with White reference, alpha=0.05 two-sided. Then: all-candidate sweep (7 candidates) comparing alone-vs-full coefficients for comparative identification; effect-scale translation (odds ratios plus analytic delta-method average marginal effects cross-checked against statsmodels get_margeff, and predicted probabilities at SES -1SD vs +1SD); a 720-specification descriptive sensitivity grid (4 SES codings x 3 race references x 3 academic sets x 4 extra-covariate sets x 5 estimators) reported as a full distribution with no selection on the target values; attenuation decomposition and leave-one-covariate-out diagnostics; VIF; events-per-variable precision audit; and a 400-replicate case-resampling bootstrap (seed 20261025) for the M3 coefficient and the M0->M3 change. The exact target pair was analysed as a scaling-versus-covariate-set question via the ratio b_full/b_alone, which is invariant to any SES rescaling. Script deleted all outputs and re-ran from a clean state to confirm reproducibility.

native_result.HypoB: The completion advantage for Black students is concentrated at the high end of the socioeconomic distribution. Raw (unadjusted) Black BA-completion rates are BELOW White rates at every SES stratum (Black 0.44/1.33/1.63/3.03% vs White 1.78/4.32/3.73/3.67% across SES quartiles; overall 1.33% vs 3.54%), so there is no unconditional advantage — but the Black-White gap narrows monotonically with SES (risk ratio 0.25, 0.31, 0.44, 0.83) and reaches statistical parity only in the top SES quartile (SES >= +0.41, ~75th percentile: RD -0.64 pp, 95% CI -2.42 to +2.30, Fisher p=0.72). Once students are compared at equal academic resources (ASVAB composite, class percentile, sex, family size), Black completion exceeds White at every level above the bottom quartile and the advantage grows with SES: adjusted RD -0.01 pp (Q1, RR 0.99), +1.51 (Q2, RR 1.52), +1.76 (Q3, RR 1.62), +3.05 pp (Q4, RR 1.91); the adequately supported pooled upper-SES-half contrast is +2.40 pp (adjusted 5.50% vs 3.10%; 95% bootstrap CI -0.03 to +4.99; RR 1.78, 0.99-2.65). A continuous adjusted-contrast curve crosses zero near SES -1.1 and has a bootstrap CI excluding zero only between SES +0.25 and +1.25 (~68th-94th percentile). Corroborated by a direct within-region adjusted logistic (upper-half OR 1.88, 1.05-3.34, p=0.033), a form-free Mantel-Haenszel OR stratified on ASVAB quintiles (upper-half-SES OR 1.82, 1.02-3.26; bottom-half-SES OR 0.86, 0.44-1.66) and a Firth penalized fit (+2.64 pp upper half, +3.32 pp top quartile). Equivalently, Black completion is far more SES-dependent than White (OR per 1 SD of SES 2.07, 1.47-2.90 vs 1.17, 1.02-1.36; slope difference z=2.99, p=0.003), so high family SES 'buys' much more BA completion for Black students. Hypothesis: the Black advantage in completion rates is most pronounced at upper socioeconomic levels — at and above roughly the 75th percentile of SES (SES >= +0.4 SD, strongest over +0.25 to +1.25) — and is absent at low SES, where Black students remain below White students at every level of resources.

native_result.query: Which two roles have the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems, with 49.6%(95% CI [49.219, 49.981] and 61.389% (95% CI [60.955, 61.822]) of respondents indicating so after bootstrapping for statistical significance?
native_result.HypoA: Project leads (49.6%, 95% CI [49.219, 49.981]) and data scientists (61.389%, 95% CI [60.955, 61.822]) have the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems after bootstrapping for statistical significance.
native_result.HypoB: The two roles are Project Lead / Project Manager and Data Scientist. In the survey's Q8 multi-select block (which records, role by role, whether a respondent's organization involves that role in addressing requirements/ML aspects), 99 of the 194 respondents who answered the block (51.031%, bootstrap 95% CI [43.81, 58.25]) named the Project Lead / Project Manager and 95 (48.969%, 95% CI [41.75, 56.19]) named the Data Scientist, with negative sentinels (-77/-99/-66/-1) treated as non-response. These two are far and away the most frequently associated roles: the third-ranked role, Business Analyst, is named by only 25.773% (95% CI [19.59, 31.96]), followed by Developer (19.072%), Solution Architect (12.371%), Requirements Engineer (10.309%) and Tester (1.031%). The pairing of the two leaders is robust - 100% of 20,000 respondent-level bootstrap replicates place Project Lead and Data Scientist as the top two, and their order is invariant across every denominator convention tested (all 276 rows: 35.87%/34.42%; 194 valid respondents: 51.03%/48.97%; completed-only 188: 51.06%/49.47%; role-reported 180: 54.44%/52.22%; respondents naming >=1 role 173: 57.23%/54.91%). The two are, however, statistically indistinguishable from each other (paired difference +2.06 pp, 95% CI [-7.73, +11.86]; McNemar exact p = 0.752), so the defensible claim is that these two roles jointly lead, not that one exceeds the other. Interpretation: responsibility for requirements in ML-enabled systems is concentrated in the project-management and data-science functions rather than in traditional requirements-engineering or testing roles - Requirements Engineer is named by only ~10% and Tester by ~1% - which suggests a requirements-ownership gap in ML-enabled system projects. Caveat: the ~49.6% figure is consistent with the Data Scientist proportion measured here, but the ~61.389% figure is not reproducible from this file (no role exceeds 57.23% under any defensible denominator), and the cited CI half-widths of +/-0.4 pp imply an effective sample of ~48,000-66,000 whereas this file has 276 respondents (1,552 respondent-role cells); honest respondent-level CIs are +/-7 pp.

native_result.query: How does the effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP compare between developing countries and countries in Sub-Saharan Africa?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it
native_result.HypoB: Increasing education expenditure is not associated with higher per-capita income in either group; where a slope is measurable it is negative in both, and it is about 6.6x steeper in raw units for the lower-middle-income ('developing') group than for Sub-Saharan Africa (-0.66 log points per +1pp of GNI, 95% CI [-1.01,-0.31], n=5, vs -0.10, 95% CI [-0.15,-0.05], n=5; raw difference -0.56, 95% CI [-0.78,-0.34], n=10) -- but that gap is a scale artefact, not a difference in sensitivity: standardised on each group's own variation the two are indistinguishable (r=-0.960 LMC vs -0.967 SSF; standardised difference +0.008, 95% CI [-0.53,+0.54], p=0.97), because SSA's education-expenditure share varied 2.9x more than LMC's in the only comparable window. This direct comparison rests on n=5 vs n=5 (2011-2015), since GNI per capita exists for Sub-Saharan Africa only from 2011. The observable channel that does differ between groups is education investment -> gross enrolment rather than -> income: SSA expanded primary gross enrolment by +36.4pp and secondary by +28.6pp over 1975-2015 while its education-expenditure share FELL 1.15pp (mean 4.30% of GNI), whereas LMC raised its share 0.37pp (mean 3.50%) for +22.7pp/+36.7pp of enrolment; in differenced terms a +1pp rise in the share predicts no enrolment gain in either group (LMC -0.78pp primary, 95% CI [-2.28,+0.71], p=0.30, n=40, and -0.79pp secondary, [-1.71,+0.14], p=0.09; SSF +0.25pp primary, [-1.27,+1.77], p=0.74, and -0.26pp secondary, [-0.91,+0.38], p=0.41; group contrasts p=0.34 and p=0.52, n=80). native_result.query: How does age influence the likelihood of withdrawing more money from savings than putting in?
native_result.HypoA: Younger individuals are more likely to withdraw more money from savings than they had put in and with a negative coefficient between age and withdrawing more than putting into savings (-0.0422).
native_result.WorkflowA:
1. One-hot encode Gender variable into MALE and FEMALE
2. Extract the independent variables ['AGE','INCOME', 'BMI', 'BLACK', 'HISPANIC', 'MALE', 'FEMALE']
3. Add dependent variable (DISSAVED) from the df
4. Add a constant term to the independent variable to account for the intercept term in the logistic regression model.

  DISSAVED = 1 if 'TOOK MORE MONEY OUT' else 0
  SAMESAVE = 1 if 'NO SAVINGS' or 'NO CHANGE' else 0

native_result.HypoB: Higher time preference (impatience), proxied by 1989 savings behaviour in NLSY79 ("Was more money put into or taken out of R/spouse savings since last interview, 1989"), predicts higher BMI measured in 1992 (n=8,503): each one-step loss of patience is associated with +0.097 BMI units (95% CI 0.017-0.177, p=0.018) and non-savers' obesity prevalence is 22.4% versus 14.0% for savers (adjusted obesity OR for savers 0.74, 95% CI 0.58-0.94, p=0.013). The association is modest (about 0.02-0.14 BMI SDs), concentrated in women (put-in -0.32 vs men -0.08) and the 14-18 age cohort (-0.44, p=0.037; age x exposure interaction p=0.037), stable across median-impute+indicators, complete-case and MICE specifications, but it is not robust to how prior adiposity is handled: it is -0.53 (p=0.002) without baseline BMI 1989 and vanishes (+0.02, p=0.93) when the outcome is the 1989-1992 change in BMI, so we hypothesise that impatience raises BMI only weakly and that most of the observed gradient reflects confounding by resources, earlier-life adiposity and reverse causality rather than a causal effect of time preference.

native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: Pottery form diversity collapsed while pottery decoration diversity increased simultaneously in the 18th century BCE (1800-1701 BCE, calBP 3750-3650; final Late Neolithic bin, immediately preceding the Older Bronze Age). Across that single 100-year step the Z-value of pottery FORM drops from +0.74 to -1.13 (dZ = -1.87 SD, the largest form decline in the 3800-year record, reaching the lower bound of the observed scale), while the Z-value of pottery DECORATION rises from -0.48 to +0.97 (dZ = +1.45 SD). This opposite-signed combination occurs in exactly 1 of 38 century steps and its mirror image (form up, decoration down) in none, while the two series are otherwise weakly positively correlated (r = +0.11) - so the simultaneity is a unique event, not an anti-correlated trend. Pottery form then remains pinned at the scale floor for the following 1200 years (level shift -1.83 SD), i.e. the change is a permanent reorganisation of formal variability rather than a single-century fluctuation, and it is not preceded or accompanied by any documented decline in the demographic/land-use proxies in these files (Belau pollen openness -0.22 SD, flat site-density KDE).
native_result.WorkflowB: Primary grid = 39 raw 100-yr Z anchors of capital.csv (the sample on which the Z standardisation was performed). Detector: simultaneous successive difference over the same 100-yr step, dZ_form <= -thr*SD and dZ_dec >= +thr*SD, thr in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}. Replication grids: 37 raw anchors of time_series_data.csv (verified identical to capital.csv, max|diff| = 0), 100-yr bin means of the linear-interpolated yearly series (w = 100/200/300 yr) and the yearly rolling-100 change series (study's pollen_grate_100-style construction). Floor robustness via MAD scaling, rank transform and deletion of the saturated plateau rows. Century assigned by year-overlap of the transition interval plus an anchor-to-bin attachment test using the periodisation labels. Pollen used as context only.

native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: PC1 of the forms of capital peaks at 1100 BCE (+4.45) and is lower in every subsequent Younger Bronze Age horizon: PC1 = 4.452 (1100 BCE), 2.172 (1000), 1.654 (900), 1.910 (800), 1.247 (700), 0.829 (600), 0.815 (500 BCE), giving six positive differences score(1100)-score(bin) of +2.280, +2.798, +2.542, +3.205, +3.623 and +3.636. The trajectory is a step-drop followed by a non-monotonic plateau with its minimum at 500 BCE, not a monotonic decline: a large immediate drop at 1000 BCE, then a low plateau of ~0.8-2.2 with a slight mid-window dip at 900 BCE and a partial rebound at 800 BCE (800 lies above 900), and the lowest values at 600-500 BCE. We therefore hypothesize that the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age was a brief maximum in overall capital accumulation and elaboration, after which capital investment fell steeply and stabilized at a low level that drifted slightly lower to its minimum at 500 BCE. The 1100 BCE excess is driven by social capital - copper/gold (ZCU_AU, +0.90 to +1.30 per contrast) and monument count (ZMonument, +0.36) - and by symbolic capital, house size (Zhausgr, +0.45 to +0.50) and dagger (ZDolch, +0.41 to +0.46), with economic capital contributing via deposits (ZHort, +0.57 to +1.25 against 900-500 BCE); cultural capital is the only negative term (-0.21), because pottery decoration rises after 1100 BCE while pottery form is unchanged. Crucially, what collapses immediately at 1000 BCE is copper-gold, house size and dagger, not deposits: ZHort stays at 3.38 at both 1100 and 1000 BCE, so the economic gap opens only from 900 BCE and widens from 700 BCE - the 1100 BCE peak is thus a metal/house/monument maximum with a one-century-long hoard-deposition tail. The pattern is not an artifact of carried-forward data (constant columns ZSichel, ZKeform and near-constant ZAxtSchwert, Zamber, ZBeil contribute -0.06 to +0.02, while all named drivers vary with sd 0.6-1.6 inside the window), it survives exact mean-0/sd-1 re-standardization (all six signs identical, bin ordering identical), and although PC1 explains only 31.8% of variance, PC2 independently marks 1100 BCE as the sole positive-score bin in the window, i.e. 1100 BCE is an outlier in the full capital space.

native_result.query: In the PCA conducted on forms of capital, analyzed in hundred-year time slices, how are the symbolic capital components such as house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords characterized in terms of their values on the first principal component (PC1) and distribution across the second principal component (PC2)?
native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB:
## Основной прогон
Корреляционная PCA на 12 формах капитала, 39 веков (4300–500 BCE, capital.csv, `decimal=','`), один глобальный PCA, loading = corr(признак, PC), знаки по вашей конвенции В5 (PC1 = «общая интенсивность/накопление»; PC2 развёрнута так, чтобы максимум |нагрузки| был положительным — якорь Axes&Celts).

**Дисперсия: PC1 = 30.3 %, PC2 = 19.5 %** (PC1+PC2 = 49.8 %; кумулятивно PC3 12.9 %, PC4 12.5 %). К ddof нечувствительно (ddof=0 vs 1: дельта 0.00 п.п., т.к. доля ev/Σev инвариантна).

### Символический капитал (correlation loadings)
| признак | PC1 | ранг \|PC1\| | PC2 | ранг \|PC2\| | eig_PC1 | eig_PC2 | \|PC2\|/\|PC1\| |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HouseSize | **+0.429** | **10/12** | **+0.500** | **5/12** | 0.225 | 0.327 | 1.17 |
| Dagger | **+0.507** | **6/12** | **+0.113** | **10/12** | 0.266 | 0.074 | 0.22 |
| HatchetSword | **+0.570** | **5/12** | **+0.082** | **12/12** | 0.299 | 0.054 | 0.15 |

Медиана |loading| по 12 признакам: PC1 0.484, PC2 0.366. Полюса PC1: Copper&Gold +0.78, Pottery Decoration +0.73, Depot +0.65 против Pottery Form −0.67, Axes&Celts −0.46, Amber −0.46, Sickle −0.29. Полюса PC2: Axes&Celts +0.72, Amber +0.68, Monument Size +0.60, Pottery Form +0.58, **House Size +0.50**, Monument Count +0.45 против Sickle −0.26, Depot −0.16.

## Три пункта, которые вы просили подсветить, а не сглаживать
1. **Знак на PC1: все три символических положительны и не «против» основной массе** — и это не следствие разворота: при правиле «большинство форм > 0» они и так были положительны, а в leave-one-century-out джекнайфе (39 прогонов) все три положительны 39/39. Более того, символическая группа — **единственная внутренне знаково-согласованная**: средние знаковые нагрузки PC1 = symbolic +0.502 (min 0.429), social +0.237, economic +0.091, cultural +0.028 (последняя растянута от −0.673 до +0.729).
2. **Развилка В6 разрешается НЕ в пользу «разнонаправленного разведения» трио по PC2** — этого в данных нет. Все три на PC2 одного знака (39/39 в джекнайфе), Dagger и HatchetSword почти коллинеарны (угол в плоскости PC1–PC2 всего 4.4°), а House Size отстоит от них на 36.8°/41.1°. То есть PC2 **ранжирует трио по величине, а не противоположает его членов**: она «забирает» house size (0.500, 5-е место из 12; PC2 даёт больше половины его двухмерной communality 0.435) и почти не трогает оружие (0.113 и 0.082 — 10-е и **самое слабое, 12-е** места из 12). Оговорка: абсолютный знак на PC2 конвенционный (зеркальная ориентация меняет все три знака сразу), относительная картина — нет.
3. **Устойчивость вывода к 39 vs 37 и к типу нагрузки — качественной инверсии нет.** 37 веков (только совпадающие с time_series_data.csv): знаки PC1 совпали 12/12, corr нагрузок PC1 = 0.996, трио = +0.336/+0.457/+0.545 (ранги 10/9/7) на PC1 и +0.512/+0.283/+0.198 (ранги 3/7/11) на PC2; PC1 32.4 %, PC2 16.4 %. Ковариационная PCA на сырых Z (ZSichel std 0.53 не ломает вывод): трио PC1 +0.431/+0.529/+0.570 (ранги 10/6/5), PC2 +0.551/+0.181/+0.101 (5/8/12). Собственный вектор vs correlation-loading: **ранги совпадают побитово, Spearman = 1.000** на обеих осях. Диапазоны LOO: HouseSize PC1 0.34–0.50 / PC2 0.45–0.58; Dagger PC1 0.44–0.57 / PC2 0.03–0.21; HatchetSword PC1 0.49–0.66 / PC2 0.03–0.14; дисперсия PC1 28.6–31.8 %, PC2 17.8–20.4 %.

**Вторичный материал (по эпохам, в тезис не выношу):** средние PC2 по столетним срезам — EN −0.70 (sd 2.26), MN +1.80 (0.47), SG +0.62 (0.37), LN −0.44 (0.50), OBA +0.69 (1.29), YBA −1.12 (0.65); общий разброс PC2 sd 1.53, диапазон [−3.65, +2.50]; PC1 по эпохам растёт: EN −1.74 → MN −1.37 → SG −1.12 → LN +0.33 → OBA +3.09 → YBA +1.85.

## Финальная гипотеза
**EN:** У PCA форм капитала, проанализированном в столетних срезах (39 веков, 4300–500 BCE; корреляционная PCA, PC1 = 30.3 %, PC2 = 19.5 % дисперсии), символические компоненты — размер дома, кинжалы и топоры-мечи — занимают на PC1 **среднюю полосу и стоят на той же («положительной», накопительской) стороне, что и основная масса форм капитала**, но не являются её двигателями: их нагрузки +0.43, +0.51 и +0.57 против +0.78 (медь/золото), +0.73 (орнамент керамики), +0.65 (клады) и медианы 0.48, т.е. ранги 10-й, 6-й и 5-й из 12 — при этом именно символическая группа оказывается единственной, где все формы согласованно положительны (средняя знаковая нагрузка +0.50, минимум 0.43), тогда как социальный, экономический и культурный капитал внутри своих групп знаково расщеплён. По PC2 символический капитал распределён **резко неравномерно, но не противоположно**: все три компоненты одного знака, и PC2 работает как ось их ранжирования — размер дома заметно уходит на PC2 (+0.50, 5-е место из 12, наравне с монументальностью: размер памятников +0.60, количество памятников +0.45, янтарь +0.68, топоры/кельты +0.72), а кинжалы и особенно топоры-мечи на PC2 практически не загружены (+0.11 и +0.08; 10-е и самое слабое 12-е место из 12) и потому остаются почти одномерным явлением на PC1. Иначе: символический капитал следует за общей осью накопления слабее «богатых» материальных индикаторов и не противостоит им, а его внутренняя дифференциация проходит не между «дома vs оружие», а по степени связанности с второй осью монументально-предметной репрезентации — house size двухосен (отношение |PC2|/|PC1| = 1.17), оружие одноосно (0.22 и 0.15). Картинка устойчива: leave-one-century-out (39/39 совпадений по всем качественным утверждениям), 37-вечная матрица, ковариационная PCA и переход от correlation-loading к собственным векторам (ранги совпадают, Spearman 1.000) её не переворачивают; абсолютные знаки PC1/PC2 конвенционны, относительные — нет.

## Ограничения
(1) PC2 менее устойчив, чем PC1: при переходе 39→37 веков совпадение знаков нагрузок PC2 10/12 (corr 0.77) против PC1 12/12 (corr 0.996) — величину «вторичных» нагрузок на PC2 надо читать с бо́льшим допуском. (2) Знаки компонент определены с точностью до общего множителя −1 по каждой оси — сообщены относительные знамена, абсолютные только при заявленной конвенции. (3) Считано, что «больше находок = выше Z»; метаданные инверсий не показывают. (4) N/ошибок датировок нет, поэтому доверительных интервалов нагрузок нет — вместо них джекнайф и скользящие окна (последние показывают сильную локальную нестабильность и потому в вывод не входят). (5) PC1 в этом наборе не чистая «интенсивность»: керамика/топоры-кельты/янтарь загружены отрицательно, так что говорить «PC1 = рост» можно только как о доминирующем, а не единственном смысле оси.

sub_hypo.relations: House size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on PC1 and widely distributed values on PC2.

sub_hypo.text: Symbolic capital—house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords—loads positively on the main accumulation axis, PC1, but is not its strongest driver. Symbolic capital is the only capital group whose members all have positive PC1 loadings; social, economic, and cultural capital are internally split in sign.
sub_hypo.context: One global correlation PCA of 12 capital forms in capital.csv, covering 39 century-level observations from 4300–500 BCE. Loadings are correlations between features and components. PC1 is oriented as general intensity/accumulation and explains 30.3% of variance, although its mixed loadings mean it is not a pure growth axis.
sub_hypo.relations: House size, daggers, and hatchets/swords have PC1 correlation loadings +0.429, +0.507, and +0.570, ranking 10th, 6th, and 5th of 12 by absolute loading; the median absolute loading is 0.484. Their positive loadings are weaker than copper/gold (+0.78), pottery decoration (+0.73), and depots (+0.65), rather than opposed to them. The symbolic group's mean signed loading is +0.502, minimum +0.429; social, economic, and cultural group means are +0.237, +0.091, and +0.028. Negative PC1 loadings include pottery form (−0.67), axes/celts (−0.46), amber (−0.46), and sickles (−0.29).

sub_hypo.text: PC2 differentiates symbolic capital by loading magnitude, not by opposing houses to weapons: house size is substantially associated with PC2, whereas daggers and especially hatchets/swords have little association with it.
sub_hypo.context: The same global correlation PCA of 12 capital forms across 39 centuries, 4300–500 BCE. PC2 explains 19.5% of variance and is oriented so its largest absolute loading, axes/celts, is positive. PC1 and PC2 together explain 49.8%.
sub_hypo.relations: PC2 loadings for house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords are all positive: +0.500, +0.113, and +0.082, ranking 5th, 10th, and 12th of 12. House size aligns with the positive monument/object-representation pole: axes/celts +0.72, amber +0.68, monument size +0.60, and monument count +0.45. Absolute PC2/PC1 loading ratios are 1.17, 0.22, and 0.15, respectively: house size is two-axis, while weapons are predominantly PC1-associated. PC2 accounts for more than half of house size's two-component communality of 0.435. Daggers and hatchets/swords are nearly collinear in the PC1–PC2 plane (4.4° apart), while house size differs from them by 36.8° and 41.1°. Absolute component signs are conventional; their relative alignment is not.

sub_hypo.text: The positive PC1 alignment and unequal, same-sign PC2 differentiation of symbolic capital are qualitatively robust to century omission, restricting the sample to overlapping centuries, covariance PCA, and using eigenvector coefficients instead of correlation loadings.
sub_hypo.context: Sensitivity analyses of the 39-century, 4300–500 BCE capital PCA: 39 leave-one-century-out runs; a 37-century subset matching time_series_data.csv; covariance PCA on raw Z values; and comparison of correlation loadings with eigenvector coefficients.
sub_hypo.relations: All three symbolic forms retain positive PC1 and same-sign PC2 loadings in 39/39 omission runs. House size, dagger, and hatchet/sword loading ranges are respectively 0.34–0.50, 0.44–0.57, and 0.49–0.66 on PC1, and 0.45–0.58, 0.03–0.21, and 0.03–0.14 on PC2. In the 37-century analysis, their PC1 loadings are +0.336/+0.457/+0.545 (ranks 10/9/7), and PC2 loadings +0.512/+0.283/+0.198 (ranks 3/7/11); explained variance is 32.4% and 16.4%. Covariance PCA gives PC1 +0.431/+0.529/+0.570 (ranks 10/6/5) and PC2 +0.551/+0.181/+0.101 (ranks 5/8/12). Eigenvector and correlation-loading rankings coincide on both axes, Spearman = 1.000. Leave-one-out explained variance ranges are 28.6–31.8% for PC1 and 17.8–20.4% for PC2; changing ddof from 0 to 1 leaves explained-variance proportions unchanged.

sub_hypo.text: The secondary-axis interpretation requires more caution than the main-axis interpretation, despite the absence of a qualitative reversal for symbolic capital.
sub_hypo.context: Comparison of the 39-century capital PCA with its 37-century overlapping subset. Interpretation assumes more findings correspond to higher Z values. Observation counts and dating errors are unavailable for loading confidence intervals; strongly unstable local rolling-window results are excluded from the conclusion.
sub_hypo.relations: Across the 39- and 37-century analyses, PC1 loading signs agree for 12/12 forms and loading correlation is 0.996; PC2 signs agree for 10/12 forms and loading correlation is 0.77. Secondary PC2 loading magnitudes are therefore less stable. Each axis can be multiplied by −1 without changing relative relationships.

This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.

## Основной прогон
Корреляционная PCA на 12 формах капитала, 39 веков (4300–500 BCE, capital.csv, `decimal=','`), один глобальный PCA, loading = corr(признак, PC), знаки по вашей конвенции В5 (PC1 = «общая интенсивность/накопление»; PC2 развёрнута так, чтобы максимум |нагрузки| был положительным — якорь Axes&Celts).

**Дисперсия: PC1 = 30.3 %, PC2 = 19.5 %** (PC1+PC2 = 49.8 %; кумулятивно PC3 12.9 %, PC4 12.5 %). К ddof нечувствительно (ddof=0 vs 1: дельта 0.00 п.п., т.к. доля ev/Σev инвариантна).

### Символический капитал (correlation loadings)
| признак | PC1 | ранг \|PC1\| | PC2 | ранг \|PC2\| | eig_PC1 | eig_PC2 | \|PC2\|/\|PC1\| |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HouseSize | **+0.429** | **10/12** | **+0.500** | **5/12** | 0.225 | 0.327 | 1.17 |
| Dagger | **+0.507** | **6/12** | **+0.113** | **10/12** | 0.266 | 0.074 | 0.22 |
| HatchetSword | **+0.570** | **5/12** | **+0.082** | **12/12** | 0.299 | 0.054 | 0.15 |

Медиана |loading| по 12 признакам: PC1 0.484, PC2 0.366. Полюса PC1: Copper&Gold +0.78, Pottery Decoration +0.73, Depot +0.65 против Pottery Form −0.67, Axes&Celts −0.46, Amber −0.46, Sickle −0.29. Полюса PC2: Axes&Celts +0.72, Amber +0.68, Monument Size +0.60, Pottery Form +0.58, **House Size +0.50**, Monument Count +0.45 против Sickle −0.26, Depot −0.16.

## Три пункта, которые вы просили подсветить, а не сглаживать
1. **Знак на PC1: все три символических положительны и не «против» основной массе** — и это не следствие разворота: при правиле «большинство форм > 0» они и так были положительны, а в leave-one-century-out джекнайфе (39 прогонов) все три положительны 39/39. Более того, символическая группа — **единственная внутренне знаково-согласованная**: средние знаковые нагрузки PC1 = symbolic +0.502 (min 0.429), social +0.237, economic +0.091, cultural +0.028 (последняя растянута от −0.673 до +0.729).
2. **Развилка В6 разрешается НЕ в пользу «разнонаправленного разведения» трио по PC2** — этого в данных нет. Все три на PC2 одного знака (39/39 в джекнайфе), Dagger и HatchetSword почти коллинеарны (угол в плоскости PC1–PC2 всего 4.4°), а House Size отстоит от них на 36.8°/41.1°. То есть PC2 **ранжирует трио по величине, а не противоположает его членов**: она «забирает» house size (0.500, 5-е место из 12; PC2 даёт больше половины его двухмерной communality 0.435) и почти не трогает оружие (0.113 и 0.082 — 10-е и **самое слабое, 12-е** места из 12). Оговорка: абсолютный знак на PC2 конвенционный (зеркальная ориентация меняет все три знака сразу), относительная картина — нет.
3. **Устойчивость вывода к 39 vs 37 и к типу нагрузки — качественной инверсии нет.** 37 веков (только совпадающие с time_series_data.csv): знаки PC1 совпали 12/12, corr нагрузок PC1 = 0.996, трио = +0.336/+0.457/+0.545 (ранги 10/9/7) на PC1 и +0.512/+0.283/+0.198 (ранги 3/7/11) на PC2; PC1 32.4 %, PC2 16.4 %. Ковариационная PCA на сырых Z (ZSichel std 0.53 не ломает вывод): трио PC1 +0.431/+0.529/+0.570 (ранги 10/6/5), PC2 +0.551/+0.181/+0.101 (5/8/12). Собственный вектор vs correlation-loading: **ранги совпадают побитово, Spearman = 1.000** на обеих осях. Диапазоны LOO: HouseSize PC1 0.34–0.50 / PC2 0.45–0.58; Dagger PC1 0.44–0.57 / PC2 0.03–0.21; HatchetSword PC1 0.49–0.66 / PC2 0.03–0.14; дисперсия PC1 28.6–31.8 %, PC2 17.8–20.4 %.

**Вторичный материал (по эпохам, в тезис не выношу):** средние PC2 по столетним срезам — EN −0.70 (sd 2.26), MN +1.80 (0.47), SG +0.62 (0.37), LN −0.44 (0.50), OBA +0.69 (1.29), YBA −1.12 (0.65); общий разброс PC2 sd 1.53, диапазон [−3.65, +2.50]; PC1 по эпохам растёт: EN −1.74 → MN −1.37 → SG −1.12 → LN +0.33 → OBA +3.09 → YBA +1.85.

## Финальная гипотеза
**EN:** У PCA форм капитала, проанализированном в столетних срезах (39 веков, 4300–500 BCE; корреляционная PCA, PC1 = 30.3 %, PC2 = 19.5 % дисперсии), символические компоненты — размер дома, кинжалы и топоры-мечи — занимают на PC1 **среднюю полосу и стоят на той же («положительной», накопительской) стороне, что и основная масса форм капитала**, но не являются её двигателями: их нагрузки +0.43, +0.51 и +0.57 против +0.78 (медь/золото), +0.73 (орнамент керамики), +0.65 (клады) и медианы 0.48, т.е. ранги 10-й, 6-й и 5-й из 12 — при этом именно символическая группа оказывается единственной, где все формы согласованно положительны (средняя знаковая нагрузка +0.50, минимум 0.43), тогда как социальный, экономический и культурный капитал внутри своих групп знаково расщеплён. По PC2 символический капитал распределён **резко неравномерно, но не противоположно**: все три компоненты одного знака, и PC2 работает как ось их ранжирования — размер дома заметно уходит на PC2 (+0.50, 5-е место из 12, наравне с монументальностью: размер памятников +0.60, количество памятников +0.45, янтарь +0.68, топоры/кельты +0.72), а кинжалы и особенно топоры-мечи на PC2 практически не загружены (+0.11 и +0.08; 10-е и самое слабое 12-е место из 12) и потому остаются почти одномерным явлением на PC1. Иначе: символический капитал следует за общей осью накопления слабее «богатых» материальных индикаторов и не противостоит им, а его внутренняя дифференциация проходит не между «дома vs оружие», а по степени связанности с второй осью монументально-предметной репрезентации — house size двухосен (отношение |PC2|/|PC1| = 1.17), оружие одноосно (0.22 и 0.15). Картинка устойчива: leave-one-century-out (39/39 совпадений по всем качественным утверждениям), 37-вечная матрица, ковариационная PCA и переход от correlation-loading к собственным векторам (ранги совпадают, Spearman 1.000) её не переворачивают; абсолютные знаки PC1/PC2 конвенционны, относительные — нет.

## Ограничения
(1) PC2 менее устойчив, чем PC1: при переходе 39→37 веков совпадение знаков нагрузок PC2 10/12 (corr 0.77) против PC1 12/12 (corr 0.996) — величину «вторичных» нагрузок на PC2 надо читать с бо́льшим допуском. (2) Знаки компонент определены с точностью до общего множителя −1 по каждой оси — сообщены относительные знамена, абсолютные только при заявленной конвенции. (3) Считано, что «больше находок = выше Z»; метаданные инверсий не показывают. (4) N/ошибок датировок нет, поэтому доверительных интервалов нагрузок нет — вместо них джекнайф и скользящие окна (последние показывают сильную локальную нестабильность и потому в вывод не входят). (5) PC1 в этом наборе не чистая «интенсивность»: керамика/топоры-кельты/янтарь загружены отрицательно, так что говорить «PC1 = рост» можно только как о доминирующем, а не единственном смысле оси.

По PC2 символический капитал распределён **резко неравномерно, но не противоположно**: все три компоненты одного знака, и PC2 работает как ось их ранжирования — размер дома заметно уходит на PC2 (+0.50, 5-е место из 12, наравне с монументальностью: размер памятников +0.60, количество памятников +0.45, янтарь +0.68, топоры/кельты +0.72), а кинжалы и особенно топоры-мечи на PC2 практически не загружены (+0.11 и +0.08; 10-е и самое слабое 12-е место из 12) и потому остаются почти одномерным явлением на PC1. Иначе: символический капитал следует за общей осью накопления слабее «богатых» материальных индикаторов и не противостоит им, а его внутренняя дифференциация проходит не между «дома vs оружие», а по степени связанности с второй осью монументально-предметной репрезентации — house size двухосен (отношение |PC2|/|PC1| = 1.17), оружие одноосно (0.22 и 0.15). Картинка устойчива: leave-one-century-out (39/39 совпадений по всем качественным утверждениям), 37-вечная матрица, ковариационная PCA и переход от correlation-loading к собственным векторам (ранги совпадают, Spearman 1.000) её не переворачивают; абсолютные знаки PC1/PC2 конвенционны, относительные — нет.

native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: Prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening varies strongly and non-randomly among the ten habitat types of the Barcelona province, and the direction depends on the denominator, so both layers are required. Among the 191 of 632 plots that actually hold non-native plants (conditional layer; region-wide 169/481 records = 35.1%), the gardening share is highest in Wetlands (55.8%, 29/52, Wilson 95% CI 42.3-68.4) and Coastal (53.5%, 23/43, 38.9-67.5), intermediate in Riparian (36.5%), Meadows (30.8%) and Urban (29.8%, 45/151, 23.1-37.5), and lowest in Croplands (18.5%, 20/108, 12.3-26.9); habitat is associated with the gardening share (binomial GLM, LR chi2 = 50.6 on 9 df, asymptotic p = 8.2e-8, permutation p = 0.0002 from 5000 habitat-label shuffles). After Holm correction over the 15 contrasts meeting the >=10-records rule: Wetlands vs Croplands (OR 5.55, p_holm < 0.0001), Coastal vs Croplands (OR 5.06, p_holm = 0.0006), Wetlands vs Urban (OR 2.97, p_holm = 0.018); Riparian vs Croplands is suggestive only (OR 2.52, p_holm = 0.054). With all 632 plots as denominator (share of plots holding at least one gardening species) the ranking shifts because encounter rate differs tenfold: Urban 47.7% (36.0-59.6), Wetlands 50.0% (34.8-65.2), Coastal 44.8% (28.4-62.5), Riparian 36.1% (25.2-48.6), Croplands 20.7% (13.6-30.0), then Meadows 7.7%, Coniferous forests 6.5%, Broad-leaved forests 4.4%, Scrublands 1.9%, Rock outcrops 0% (0/57, 0-6.3); this association is stronger (LR chi2 = 146.9, 9 df, permutation p = 0.0002; 24 of 45 pairs Holm-significant). For Broad-leaved forests (4/4), Coniferous forests (7/8), Scrublands (2/5) and Rock outcrops (0/1) habitat-level record totals are 1-8, so their apparent 100%/87.5%/40%/0% is descriptive only and its direction is not interpreted - 0% in Rock outcrops means one non-native record in 57 plots, not absence of gardening introductions. Interpretation (labelled as interpretation): the pattern is consistent with gardening-derived species dominating the non-native pool where the overall non-native load is small but ornamental propagule pressure is near (waterways, wetlands, coasts), whereas the cropland pool is dominated by the unintentional seed-contaminant pathway (76.9% of its records); jointly the two layers imply gardening species are most likely to be encountered at all in urban and wetland habitats, while cropland records are the least gardening-derived. This is a post-hoc description, not a confirmatory test, and no causal verb is intended: there is no survey-effort variable and habitat is nearly collinear with the urbanisation gradient (mean urban cover, 1000 m buffer: Urban 0.50 vs Meadows 0.03), so habitat is not separable from that gradient in these data.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inventory (work/01_inspect.py, work/02_diag.py): discovered the two .csv files are TAB-separated; verified 632 plots (unique lon/lat), 10 habitat labels, zero NA, n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo == n.total in 632/632 rows, 441/632 plots with n.total=0, and absence of any species x habitat matrix (so the species table is context only, and the Newick tree is unused because the unit of analysis is the plot). 2) Two-layer descriptives with Wilson CIs (outputs/table1_descriptive_by_habitat.csv) and pathway composition per habitat (table6). 3) Main inference: binomial-logit GLM cbind(n.gard, n.other) ~ C(habitat) on the 191 plots with n.total>0, 10 levels, reference Urban, separated levels flagged (table2); omnibus LRT chi2=50.6 (9 df) plus 5000-permutation omnibus using a closed-form one-way binomial LR statistic verified to equal the GLM deviance difference (p=0.0002). 4) Post-hoc Fisher contrasts with Holm restricted to habitats with sum(n.total)>=10 (table3), and the same for the unconditional layer across all 10 habitats (table7). 5) Sensitivity/robustness (table4): presence-response on all 632 plots, quasi-binomial dispersion (scale 0.541, deviance/df 1.204, no overdispersion), collapsed semi-natural 5-level run, and covariate-adjusted runs with elevation + log(distance.road) + urban.2009.1000m / urban.2009.50m / cropland.2009.1000m. 6) Dominant-species check (top-3 gardening species = 28.8% of gardening records) and drop-one-plot jackknife of key contrasts (table8). 7) ASCII forest plot with Wilson CIs (figure1), headline stats (summary.json), manifest (README.md), hypothesis (hypothesis.md).

native_result.HypoB: Городское землепользование значимо смещает состав интродукционных pathway (joint pathway x urban.2009.500m F=7.32, p=7e-4; delta_urban.1000m F=6.93, p=1e-3), но характер зависимости различается по pathway. (1) 'Gardening' связан с урбанизацией исторически-временнó, а не локально: доля выросла с 0.168 до 0.752 между Before 1500 и 1985-2019 (OR за период 2.30 [1.99-2.65], p=6e-30 по temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv, где городская переменная отсутствует и introduction.period служит лишь прокси эры), при нулевой локальной связи с городским покрытием (beta=-0.036 [-0.090;0.017] по urban.2009.500m; r(n.gard, urban.2009.500m)=-0.035): город генерирует поток декоративных интродукций, но не концентрирует их в инвентаризованных plot'ах. (2) 'Unintentional' - единственный pathway с положительным наклоном к фактическому городскому покрытию (beta=+0.032..+0.033 на 10 п.п. urban.2009.500m; предсказанная доля 0.543 -> 0.642 между квартилями; bootstrap разность долей +0.101 [0.035;0.173]), однако связь слабая: незначима с ковариатами, частично зеркальна падению AgriForest (три разности долей суммируются в 0) и воспроизводится на cropland (beta>0 в 18/18 прогонов), поэтому это отклик на открытые/нарушенные местообитания, а не доказанный именно городской сигнал. (3) 'AgriForest' - единственный pathway со статистически поддерживаемой и urban-специфичной ОБРАТНОЙ связью: beta=-0.255 [-0.429;-0.082] по urban.2009.500m и beta=-0.368 [-0.612;-0.124] по delta_urban.1000m (1956->2009), тогда как на cropland эффект почти исчезает (медиана -0.026), плюс сильный временнóй упадок 0.514 -> 0.061 (Fisher p=3.6e-27, n=161) - агролесохозяйственные интродукции связаны с незастроенными сельскими ландшафтами и вытесняются городским землепользованием; из-за 23 записей на 21 plot'е это направление, а не причинный вывод. Общий уровень инвазии ('есть ли хоть один инвайдер') растёт с городским покрытием без контроля местообитания (beta=+0.266, OR=1.31 на 10 п.п.), но этот эффект исчезает при учёте habitat (beta=+0.062, p=0.39), то есть объяснённым самим классом местообитания, и потому в вывод не входит. Всё это ассоциации наблюдательных данных; PGLS неприменим (в invasion_success_pathways.csv нет ни одной ландшафтной переменной и нет ключа вид<->plot).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Инспекция (inspection_pathways.py): оба 'csv' файла实际上 TSV; 632 plot (191 занятых, 441 пустых), pathway задан counts n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo; 0 NA; в invasion_success_pathways.csv переменных ландшафта нет вообще, 4 дубликата (77 видов); дерево 81 tip полностью совпадает с phylo.tip.label, все 158 длин ветвей положительны. 2) Временнóй срез: доли pathway по 4 периодам с Wilson CI, chi2, ordered binomial-logit тренд, Fisher для AgriForest. 3) Основной срез: multinomial-Poisson (plot x pathway long format, count ~ C(pathway)*urban + covariates, offset log(n.total), offset log(n.total)), квазипуассон; модели M1 (без ковариат), M2 (ковариаты без habitat), M3 (+habitat), M4 (без Urban-habitat plot'ов); pathway-specific β и 95% CI через явные контрасты и协вариационную матрицу; joint Wald/F тест взаимодействия pathway x urban. 4) Предсказанный состав на квартилях urban + cluster-bootstrap 300 повторов по plot'ам. 5) Робастность: NB2 (alpha по profile loglik), HC1-робастный Пуассон, hurdle (binomial на всех 632 plot + состав на 191). 6) Изменение ландшафта: калибровка ярлыков через correlation с delta_urban, затем модели по delta_urban (50/500/1000 м, оба варианта habitat) и по прогрессивным/регрессивным долям. 7) Чувствительность: 9 буфер x год x {urban, cropland} x {без/с habitat} = 36 прогонов, компактная таблица β/CI/доля нулей. 8) Мощность AgriForest: MDE80=2.8*SE по каждому буферу и для M4. 9) Глобальные тесты состава: multinomial chi2 по терцилям urban и PERMANOVA (Bray-Curtis, 999 перестановок, стратифицированно по habitat). 10) Опциональный phylo-appendix (own Newick parser, patristic PERMANOVA на 77 видах) - помечен как answering a different question и в вывод не входит.

sub_hypo.context: Observational data on non-native plants in Barcelona province: 632 plots, including 191 occupied plots used for pathway-composition analysis; counts are normalized by n.total.
sub_hypo.relations: Joint pathway-by-urban-cover interaction: F=7.32, p=0.0007 for urban.2009.500m; F=6.93, p=0.001 for delta_urban.1000m, defined as urban.2009.1000m minus urban.1956.1000m. These are associations, not causal effects.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening introductions increased strongly across historical periods, but this temporal pattern does not directly demonstrate an urbanization effect.
sub_hypo.context: Temporal introduction-pathway data for non-native flora in Catalonia, across four periods from Before 1500 to 1985–2019; urban cover is absent and introduction.period is only an era proxy.
sub_hypo.relations: The Gardening share increased from 0.168 to 0.752; ordered binomial-logit OR per period=2.30, 95% CI [1.99, 2.65], p=6e-30. The hypothesized historical association with urbanization is indirect.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening introductions show no supported local association with urban cover in inventoried plots, despite their strong historical increase.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants in inventoried plots in Barcelona province; local urban cover measured in 2009 within 500 m.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening composition has beta=-0.036, 95% CI [-0.090, 0.017], and r(n.gard, urban.2009.500m)=-0.035. The hypothesized urban generation of ornamental introductions is not accompanied by their local concentration in sampled plots.

sub_hypo.text: Unintentional introductions are the only pathway with a positive slope against actual urban cover, but the weak association is not demonstrably urban-specific.
sub_hypo.context: Occupied plots in Barcelona province; urban-cover quartile predictions and 300 plot-cluster bootstrap replicates, with covariate adjustment and cropland sensitivity analyses.
sub_hypo.relations: Beta=+0.032 to +0.033 per 10 percentage points of urban.2009.500m; predicted share increases from 0.543 to 0.642 between urban-cover quartiles, with bootstrap difference +0.101 [0.035, 0.173]. The association is nonsignificant with covariates, partly mirrors declining AgriForest shares because the three share differences sum to zero, and is positive for cropland in 18/18 runs. It is interpreted as an association with open/disturbed habitats rather than a proven specifically urban signal.

sub_hypo.text: AgriForest introductions have the only statistically supported, urban-specific inverse association with urban cover and historical urban expansion.
sub_hypo.context: Observational plots in Barcelona province; AgriForest has only 23 records across 21 plots, supporting a direction of association rather than a causal conclusion.
sub_hypo.relations: AgriForest beta=-0.255, 95% CI [-0.429, -0.082], for urban.2009.500m, and beta=-0.368, 95% CI [-0.612, -0.124], for the 1956–2009 urban-cover change within 1000 m. The cropland effect nearly disappears, with median beta=-0.026. This supports an association with unbuilt rural landscapes and declining representation under urban land use, not demonstrated causal displacement.

sub_hypo.text: AgriForest introductions show a strong historical decline in their share of introductions.
sub_hypo.context: Temporal introduction-pathway data for non-native flora in Catalonia, comparing Before 1500 with 1985–2019; Fisher comparison n=161.
sub_hypo.relations: The AgriForest share declines from 0.514 to 0.061; Fisher p=3.6e-27.

sub_hypo.text: The positive association between urban cover and the presence of any invader disappears after habitat adjustment and is excluded from the substantive conclusion.
sub_hypo.context: Hurdle-model occurrence component across all 632 Barcelona province plots: 191 occupied and 441 empty.
sub_hypo.relations: For presence defined as n.total>0, the unadjusted urban-cover beta is +0.266, OR=1.31 per 10 percentage points. With habitat adjustment, beta=+0.062, p=0.39; the hypothesis attributes the unadjusted association to habitat class rather than an independent urban-cover effect.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Городское землепользование значимо смещает состав интродукционных pathway (joint pathway x urban.2009.500m F=7.32, p=7e-4; delta_urban.1000m F=6.93, p=1e-3), но характер зависимости различается по pathway. (1) 'Gardening' связан с урбанизацией исторически-временнó, а не локально: доля выросла с 0.168 до 0.752 между Before 1500 и 1985-2019 (OR за период 2.30 [1.99-2.65], p=6e-30 по temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv, где городская переменная отсутствует и introduction.period служит лишь прокси эры), при нулевой локальной связи с городским покрытием (beta=-0.036 [-0.090;0.017] по urban.2009.500m; r(n.gard, urban.2009.500m)=-0.035): город генерирует поток декоративных интродукций, но не концентрирует их в инвентаризованных plot'ах. (2) 'Unintentional' - единственный pathway с положительным наклоном к фактическому городскому покрытию (beta=+0.032..+0.033 на 10 п.п. urban.2009.500m; предсказанная доля 0.543 -> 0.642 между квартилями; bootstrap разность долей +0.101 [0.035;0.173]), однако связь слабая: незначима с ковариатами, частично зеркальна падению AgriForest (три разности долей суммируются в 0) и воспроизводится на cropland (beta>0 в 18/18 прогонов), поэтому это отклик на открытые/нарушенные местообитания, а не доказанный именно городской сигнал. (3) 'AgriForest' - единственный pathway со статистически поддерживаемой и urban-специфичной ОБРАТНОЙ связью: beta=-0.255 [-0.429;-0.082] по urban.2009.500m и beta=-0.368 [-0.612;-0.124] по delta_urban.1000m (1956->2009), тогда как на cropland эффект почти исчезает (медиана -0.026), плюс сильный временнóй упадок 0.514 -> 0.061 (Fisher p=3.6e-27, n=161) - агролесохозяйственные интродукции связаны с незастроенными сельскими ландшафтами и вытесняются городским землепользованием; из-за 23 записей на 21 plot'е это направление, а не причинный вывод. Общий уровень инвазии ('есть ли хоть один инвайдер') растёт с городским покрытием без контроля местообитания (beta=+0.266, OR=1.31 на 10 п.п.), но этот эффект исчезает при учёте habitat (beta=+0.062, p=0.39), то есть объяснённым самим классом местообитания, и потому в вывод не входит. Всё это ассоциации наблюдательных данных; PGLS неприменим (в invasion_success_pathways.csv нет ни одной ландшафтной переменной и нет ключа вид<->plot).

sub_hypo.text: Relative effect shrinkage is strongest in Social psychology, where replications retain about 22% of the original effect magnitude, versus about 67–70% in Cognitive psychology and Experimental Economics.

sub_hypo.relations: The replicated proportion is 0.206 in Social, compared with 0.471 in Cognitive and 0.611 in Economics.

sub_hypo.text: Cognitive psychology and Experimental Economics are similar on both absolute-gap and relative-shrinkage metrics.

sub_hypo.text: The numerically larger absolute gap in Cognitive psychology reflects larger original effects rather than stronger proportional shrinkage.

На колонке оригинальных авторов (seniority.o) доля assistant-рангов равна 0/35 — артефакт прочтения «про оригиналов», а не находка.

native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: Original papers in the Experimental Economics replication project are on average 28.0 pages long (n = 18 unique originals, range 16-45), while original papers in the Psychology (RPP) project average 11.2 pages (n = 95 unique originals, range 1-31) - Experimental Economics originals are about 2.5x longer (difference 16.8 pages, Welch 95% CI 12.9-20.6, p ~ 7e-09; median ratio ~3x). Length = number of pages of the original article, not words; only projects 'ee' and 'rpp' were analysed (ml1/ml3 Many Labs and Social/Cognitive disciplines excluded). The gap is explained by publication format (economics originals are full-length AER/QJE articles with theory, appendices and econometric tables; psychology originals are short single-effect reports in PS/JPSP), plus a page-coding artifact behind a few very short RPP records. The estimate is robust to averaging over unique originals vs O/R rows (28.0 vs 11.2), to dropping the single implausible 1-page RPP record (rpp mean 11.3), and to restricting to length>2 (2.4x).
native_result.WorkflowB: pandas load of meta-regression_study_data CSV -> filter project in {ee, rpp} (115 O/R rows) -> deduplicate to unique original articles by (title, authors.o, pub_year) -> ee n=18, rpp n=95 -> per-project descriptives (mean, SD, median, IQR, range, 95% t-CI plus 10k bootstrap CI) -> Welch t-test, bootstrap CI and ratio for the ee-rpp difference -> sensitivity analyses (row-level averaging; exclude rpp.53 length=1; restrict to length>2) -> heuristic label cross-check against replication-success CSV (no joins, no length from it). Script: analysis.py; numeric log: out/analysis_log.txt

Within race x sex cells, later jail is associated with a median wealth shortfall of $4,300 among Hispanic men ($700 vs $5,000; ratio 0.14; MWU p=0.00012, Cliff's delta -0.32) and $3,500 among white men ($2,000 vs $5,500; ratio 0.36; p=0.029, delta -0.17), but only $700 among Black men ($800 vs $1,500; ratio 0.53; p=0.082, delta -0.09, CI touching zero). Because never-jailed Black men already hold $1,500 - less than the $2,000 held by jailed white men - the floor reached by incarcerated respondents of every race ($700-$2,000) is compressed enough that race ordering within the incarcerated group is not resolvable (Black vs white jailed men -$1,200, 95% CI -$4,680 to +$600, p=0.15; Hispanic vs white -$1,300, CI -$5,000 to +$1,400, p=0.19; Black vs Hispanic +$100, p=0.87), while the sex axis inside the incarcerated group does separate: pooled jailed women (n=37) have median $0 vs $1,000 for pooled jailed men (n=252) (gap -$1,000, CI -$1,400 to -$260, p=0.024, delta -0.22). That sex gap reflects zero-dominance rather than debt: 64.9% of jailed women report exactly $0, rising to 81.2% of jailed Black women (n=16) and 77.8% of jailed Hispanic women (n=9), cells whose medians are structurally pinned at 0 and must not be read as magnitudes. The incarceration shortfall is not a bottom-only artifact: median deficits widen monotonically up the distribution (p25 $0, p50 -$2,880, p75 -$10,100, p90 -$49,610) while relative ratios stay flat (0.20-0.37), i.e. a multiplicative compression of wealth, and it widens after 1985 (overall gap -$2,880 in 1985, -$10,500 in 1990, -$8,500 in 1996, jailed medians $0 in every race cell by 1990). Framing: 1985 wealth is measured at or before most jail spells, so this is a prospective association - low 1985 wealth as a precursor marker of later jail, not a causal effect of incarceration on 1985 wealth. Because jail is self-reported (understating exposure and biasing contrasts toward the null) and the extract contains no survey weights, covariates, or residence/group-quarters field to identify incarceration any other way, these magnitudes are descriptive lower bounds.

Because never-jailed Black men already hold $1,500 - less than the $2,000 held by jailed white men - the floor reached by incarcerated respondents of every race ($700-$2,000) is compressed enough that race ordering within the incarcerated group is not resolvable (Black vs white jailed men -$1,200, 95% CI -$4,680 to +$600, p=0.15; Hispanic vs white -$1,300, CI -$5,000 to +$1,400, p=0.19; Black vs Hispanic +$100, p=0.87), while the sex axis inside the incarcerated group does separate: pooled jailed women (n=37) have median $0 vs $1,000 for pooled jailed men (n=252) (gap -$1,000, CI -$1,400 to -$260, p=0.024, delta -0.22). That sex gap reflects zero-dominance rather than debt: 64.9% of jailed women report exactly $0, rising to 81.2% of jailed Black women (n=16) and 77.8% of jailed Hispanic women (n=9), cells whose medians are structurally pinned at 0 and must not be read as magnitudes. The incarceration shortfall is not a bottom-only artifact: median deficits widen monotonically up the distribution (p25 $0, p50 -$2,880, p75 -$10,100, p90 -$49,610) while relative ratios stay flat (0.20-0.37), i.e. a multiplicative compression of wealth, and it widens after 1985 (overall gap -$2,880 in 1985, -$10,500 in 1990, -$8,500 in 1996, jailed medians $0 in every race cell by 1990). Framing: 1985 wealth is measured at or before most jail spells, so this is a prospective association - low 1985 wealth as a precursor marker of later jail, not a causal effect of incarceration on 1985 wealth. Because jail is self-reported (understating exposure and biasing contrasts toward the null) and the extract contains no survey weights, covariates, or residence/group-quarters field to identify incarceration any other way, these magnitudes are descriptive lower bounds.

native_result.query: Between which years did the largest increases in median wealth occur among black females?
native_result.HypoA: The largest increases in median wealth from 1985 to 1990 were among black females, with a percentage increase of 1385.71%.
native_result.HypoB: Interval label: 1985-1990. Among pooled black females (n=1,548; 1,548 respondents observed in each of 1985, 1990 and 1996) median composite wealth rose from $175 in 1985 to $2,600 in 1990 and to $4,000 in 1996, so both candidate intervals are increases and the larger absolute increase occurred between 1985 and 1990 (+$2,425) rather than between 1990 and 1996 (+$1,400), a point difference of $1,025. The supporting percentage changes are +1,385.7% for 1985-1990 and +53.8% for 1990-1996, but the 1985-1990 percentage is not meaningful because the 1985 median of $175 is effectively zero. This conclusion is not robust to how exact-zero wealth values are handled: treating zeros as technical missing (medians $3,832 -> $8,100 -> $19,800; +$4,268 vs +$11,700) or restricting to positive wealth ($4,800 -> $11,057 -> $25,050; +$6,257 vs +$13,993) both reverse the ranking and give 1990-1996 as the interval with the largest increase, on both the absolute and the relative criterion. The 1985-1990 result therefore rests on 39.9% zero-coded 1985 wealth values and on the 1985 median sitting at the edge of a block in which 47.5% of black females are at or below $0; 231 black females report 0 wealth in all three waves, and zero shares roughly double in 1996 for white respondents (20.7/20.3 -> 42.6% and 24.6/25.7 -> 43.3%), which suggests part of the zeros are technical rather than real. A single bootstrap (B=2,000, primary branch) leaves 1985-1990 winning with probability 96.6%, so sampling noise is not what drives the disagreement - the zero-handling rule is. All estimates are unweighted, nominal-dollar point estimates (no weights or variance information exist in the file), no inflation adjustment is applied, rows are assumed to be distinct respondents without deduplication, and the stratification by ever_jailed is not interpretable (n=16).

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Interval label: 1985-1990. Among pooled black females (n=1,548; 1,548 respondents observed in each of 1985, 1990 and 1996) median composite wealth rose from $175 in 1985 to $2,600 in 1990 and to $4,000 in 1996, so both candidate intervals are increases and the larger absolute increase occurred between 1985 and 1990 (+$2,425) rather than between 1990 and 1996 (+$1,400), a point difference of $1,025. The supporting percentage changes are +1,385.7% for 1985-1990 and +53.8% for 1990-1996, but the 1985-1990 percentage is not meaningful because the 1985 median of $175 is effectively zero. This conclusion is not robust to how exact-zero wealth values are handled: treating zeros as technical missing (medians $3,832 -> $8,100 -> $19,800; +$4,268 vs +$11,700) or restricting to positive wealth ($4,800 -> $11,057 -> $25,050; +$6,257 vs +$13,993) both reverse the ranking and give 1990-1996 as the interval with the largest increase, on both the absolute and the relative criterion. The 1985-1990 result therefore rests on 39.9% zero-coded 1985 wealth values and on the 1985 median sitting at the edge of a block in which 47.5% of black females are at or below $0; 231 black females report 0 wealth in all three waves, and zero shares roughly double in 1996 for white respondents (20.7/20.3 -> 42.6% and 24.6/25.7 -> 43.3%), which suggests part of the zeros are technical rather than real. A single bootstrap (B=2,000, primary branch) leaves 1985-1990 winning with probability 96.6%, so sampling noise is not what drives the disagreement - the zero-handling rule is. All estimates are unweighted, nominal-dollar point estimates (no weights or variance information exist in the file), no inflation adjustment is applied, rows are assumed to be distinct respondents without deduplication, and the stratification by ever_jailed is not interpretable (n=16).

Рост доли богатства у богатых не подтверждён: доля верхнего 1 % упала с 23.1 % до 18.2 % и с 22.1 % до 18.2 %, доли top20/top10 не выросли значимо. native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (ever jailed 1985-1994) had significantly lower composite wealth than those without in all three surveyed years (1985, 1990, 1996): one-sided Mann-Whitney p = 8.0e-11, 3.9e-35, 4.6e-26; bootstrap 95% CIs for both mean and median differences exclude zero in every year; Cliff's delta -0.22 to -0.42; robust to deduplication and winsorization with mean- and median-based estimates agreeing in sign. The post-window interpretation (wealth penalty of incarceration) is defensible only for 1990 and 1996; 1985 is partially pre-treatment and reflects a pre-existing wealth gap. Absolute nominal gap is largest in 1996, rank-based effect strongest in 1990. Comparisons are unadjusted and jail concentration among black males implies likely race/sex confounding.

On this proxy the Black vs non-Black non-Hispanic difference is SES-conditional, not a constant advantage. At the lowest family-of-origin SES level (index from parental occupation white/blue at 14, mother's and father's grades, per-capita family net income 1979) Black and comparison respondents participate at statistically indistinguishable rates (4.0% vs 3.4%, +0.6pp, 95% CI -0.9..+2.2; +3.5pp, p=0.0001 once sex and ASVAB achievement are held constant); at the middle level the gap is -3.0pp; at the highest level -7.9pp (11.4% vs 19.3%). Hypothesis: rising family socioeconomic status converts into college participation far less efficiently for Black students than for their non-Black non-Hispanic peers, so any Black advantage is confined to the lowest-SES families, is not distinguishable from parity in the raw data, and is extinguished and then reversed as SES rises. native_result.query: How does the median wealth of white individuals compare to that of black and Hispanic individuals from 1985 onwards?
native_result.HypoA: 1985 onwards, white individuals have a significantly higher median wealth compared to black and Hispanic individuals.
native_result.HypoB: Among NLSY79 respondents, median family net wealth of non-black non-Hispanic ("white") respondents exceeded that of black and Hispanic respondents in every observed wave, and the gap widened monotonically across the only three wealth waves the file contains (1985, 1990, 1996 - "1985 onwards" here is three points, not a continuous trend). In constant 1996 USD (per-wave, unweighted, zeros and debts retained): white $5,104 (1985) -> $15,572 (1990) -> $42,600 (1996); black $2,333 -> $5,762 -> $9,800; Hispanic $729 -> $1,921 -> $2,562 (n = 5,774/1,699/2,631; 5,336/1,528/2,431; 3,557/1,368/2,114). The white/black median ratio was 2.19 [95% CI 1.83-2.47] -> 2.70 [2.31-3.25] -> 4.35 [3.70-5.20] and the white/Hispanic ratio 7.00 [5.70-8.75] -> 8.11 [6.36-9.13] -> 16.62 [13.83-21.30]; these ratios are scale-free, so they hold unchanged in nominal dollars, while the dollar gaps were $1,900 -> $8,172 -> $32,800 (white-black) and $3,000 -> $11,372 -> $40,038 (white-Hispanic) in nominal USD, i.e. the widening is fully visible without deflation; restating in 1996 USD only rescales the early waves (deflators 1.458 for 1985, 1.200 for 1990) to $2,771 -> $9,810 -> $32,800 and $4,375 -> $13,652 -> $40,038 - direction and ordering are identical in both money series. Every group's median rose in real terms (1985->1996: white +735%, black +320%, Hispanic +251%), so the divergence is relative: white wealth grew roughly twice as fast as black and nearly three times as fast as Hispanic. The distribution corroborates this: net wealth was <= 0 for 19.2/16.4/10.9% of white families versus 28.4/25.5/20.8% of black families (-9 to -10 pp) and 41.9/33.8/34.9% of Hispanic families (-17 to -24 pp). Caveats: this is family-level net wealth of the respondent/spouse (in 1985, respondents were only 20-28, so many are parental households), unweighted, with black and Hispanic oversamples (15.8% and 25.0% of the sample), so absolute levels are not US-representative even though group contrasts remain informative; wealth is observed for 76.9% of whites versus 84.9% of blacks and 82.9% of Hispanics in 1985, falling to 47.4% versus 68.3% and 66.6% in 1996 (only 61.6% of the 1985-observed whites versus ~80% of blacks/Hispanics remain observed), so waves are partly different people - yet the balanced panel of 5,739 respondents with all three waves gives the same ordering and slightly LARGER ratios (1996: 4.69 white/black, 17.75 white/Hispanic), because white 1996 medians are flat across retention groups ($42,600 stayers vs $42,000 non-stayers) while non-staying black/Hispanic respondents were richer ($11,918/$4,500 vs stayers $9,075/$2,400); differential attrition therefore understates rather than inflates the 1996 gap. Finally, the white/Hispanic ratio is not scale-robust (the Hispanic median sits one reporting-rounding step above zero; positive-wealth-only medians cut it to 2.24 in 1985 and 5.17 in 1996, while the dollar gap is stable at $4,520 and $43,000), so for that contrast the absolute difference and the share with non-positive wealth are the load-bearing statistics; the apparent top-coding at the maxima (84 observations at $1,321,099 in 1990 and 141 at $1,232,183 in 1996) is a plausible interpretation, not a documented fact, and it shifts means but leaves medians and 5%-trimmed medians unchanged.

In constant 1996 USD (per-wave, unweighted, zeros and debts retained): white $5,104 (1985) -> $15,572 (1990) -> $42,600 (1996); black $2,333 -> $5,762 -> $9,800; Hispanic $729 -> $1,921 -> $2,562 (n = 5,774/1,699/2,631; 5,336/1,528/2,431; 3,557/1,368/2,114). The white/black median ratio was 2.19 [95% CI 1.83-2.47] -> 2.70 [2.31-3.25] -> 4.35 [3.70-5.20] and the white/Hispanic ratio 7.00 [5.70-8.75] -> 8.11 [6.36-9.13] -> 16.62 [13.83-21.30]; these ratios are scale-free, so they hold unchanged in nominal dollars, while the dollar gaps were $1,900 -> $8,172 -> $32,800 (white-black) and $3,000 -> $11,372 -> $40,038 (white-Hispanic) in nominal USD, i.e. the widening is fully visible without deflation; restating in 1996 USD only rescales the early waves (deflators 1.458 for 1985, 1.200 for 1990) to $2,771 -> $9,810 -> $32,800 and $4,375 -> $13,652 -> $40,038 - direction and ordering are identical in both money series. Every group's median rose in real terms (1985->1996: white +735%, black +320%, Hispanic +251%), so the divergence is relative: white wealth grew roughly twice as fast as black and nearly three times as fast as Hispanic. The distribution corroborates this: net wealth was <= 0 for 19.2/16.4/10.9% of white families versus 28.4/25.5/20.8% of black families (-9 to -10 pp) and 41.9/33.8/34.9% of Hispanic families (-17 to -24 pp). Caveats: this is family-level net wealth of the respondent/spouse (in 1985, respondents were only 20-28, so many are parental households), unweighted, with black and Hispanic oversamples (15.8% and 25.0% of the sample), so absolute levels are not US-representative even though group contrasts remain informative; wealth is observed for 76.9% of whites versus 84.9% of blacks and 82.9% of Hispanics in 1985, falling to 47.4% versus 68.3% and 66.6% in 1996 (only 61.6% of the 1985-observed whites versus ~80% of blacks/Hispanics remain observed), so waves are partly different people - yet the balanced panel of 5,739 respondents with all three waves gives the same ordering and slightly LARGER ratios (1996: 4.69 white/black, 17.75 white/Hispanic), because white 1996 medians are flat across retention groups ($42,600 stayers vs $42,000 non-stayers) while non-staying black/Hispanic respondents were richer ($11,918/$4,500 vs stayers $9,075/$2,400); differential attrition therefore understates rather than inflates the 1996 gap. Finally, the white/Hispanic ratio is not scale-robust (the Hispanic median sits one reporting-rounding step above zero; positive-wealth-only medians cut it to 2.24 in 1985 and 5.17 in 1996, while the dollar gap is stable at $4,520 and $43,000), so for that contrast the absolute difference and the share with non-positive wealth are the load-bearing statistics; the apparent top-coding at the maxima (84 observations at $1,321,099 in 1990 and 141 at $1,232,183 in 1996) is a plausible interpretation, not a documented fact, and it shifts means but leaves medians and 5%-trimmed medians unchanged.

Comapring: GoldH: From 1985 onwards, white individuals have significantly higher median wealth than black and Hispanic individuals., GoldC: NLSY79 participants from 1985 onwards, with family net wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
GenH: White respondents had higher median family net wealth than black and Hispanic respondents in each observed wealth wave, and both absolute and relative gaps widened monotonically across 1985, 1990, and 1996., GenC: NLSY79 respondents with observed wealth in each wave; unweighted family-level respondent/spouse wealth, retaining zeros and debts. White means non-black non-Hispanic. These are three discrete observations, not a continuous trend. Constant-1996 USD uses assumed external CPI-U multipliers of 1.458 for 1985 and 1.200 for 1990. Per-wave white/black/Hispanic sample sizes are 5,774/1,699/2,631, 5,336/1,528/2,431, and 3,557/1,368/2,114. Respondents were aged 20–28 in 1985, with many in parental households; black and Hispanic oversamples and lack of weighting mean absolute levels are not US-representative.

native_result.query: Which two roles have the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems, with 49.6%(95% CI [49.219, 49.981] and 61.389% (95% CI [60.955, 61.822]) of respondents indicating so after bootstrapping for statistical significance?
native_result.HypoA: Project leads (49.6%, 95% CI [49.219, 49.981]) and data scientists (61.389%, 95% CI [60.955, 61.822]) have the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems after bootstrapping for statistical significance.
native_result.HypoB:
Основной прогон готов. Ответ: **Project Lead / Project Manager и Data Scientist**.

## Ответ с цифрами (M1, база = 194 респондентов, реально ответивших на блок Q8)
| rank | role | k | n | share, 95% CI (bootstrap B=10 000, seed=42, percentile) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Project Lead / Project Manager | 99 | 194 | **51.031% [43.814, 58.247]** |
| 2 | Data Scientist | 95 | 194 | **48.969% [41.753, 56.186]** |
| 3 | Business Analyst | 50 | 194 | 25.773% [19.588, 31.959] |
| 4 | Developer | 37 | 194 | 19.072% [13.918, 24.742] |
| 5 | Solution Architect | 24 | 194 | 12.371% [7.732, 17.010] |
| 6 | Requirements Engineer | 20 | 194 | 10.309% [6.186, 14.433] |
| 7 | Others (free text) | 19 | 194 | 9.794% [5.670, 13.918] |
| 8 | Test Manager / Tester | 2 | 194 | 1.031% [0.000, 2.577] |

BCa почти совпадает с percentile (PL: BCa [43.814, 57.732], normal [44.036, 58.026]; DS: BCa [41.753, 55.670]) — CI широкий не из-за метода, а из-за n=194 (bootstrap SE 3.57/3.65 pp).

## Топ-2 именно как *пара* (парный bootstrap на тех же ресемплах)
- PL vs DS: diff = +2.06 pp, CI [−7.732, +11.340], p = 0.713 → эти две роли **статистически неразличимы**, корректно называть пару, а не «PL №1».
- DS vs BA: +23.196 pp, CI [13.402, 32.990], p = 0.0001; PL vs BA: +25.258 pp, CI [15.979, 34.021], p = 0.0001 → отрыв от третьего места реален.
- Ранжирование устойчиво по всем 4 базам: 276 (35.87/34.42), 194 (51.03/48.97), 188 (51.06/49.47), 173 (57.23/54.91); зазор до rank3 = 16.3–26.0 pp.

## Reading про «association» (зафиксировано в hypothesis)
«Association with requirements» = роль отмечена `quoted` в `Q8_ML_Addressing_<role>` — единственная ролево-requirements переменная в файле. `D14_ML_Purpose_Association` = association rule learning: 11.594% (32/276), по ролям 8.065–18.182% — к вопросу отношения не имеет, в ответ не использовалось.

## Дисклеймер про 49.6% / 61.389% (без подгонки)
- Ничего не двигал: ни знаменатель, ни метрику, ни free-text. 49.6% аппроксимируется только Data Scientist (48.969% при n=194 / 49.468% при n=188); 61.389% не даёт ни одна роль ни при одной базе.
- Целевые CI невозможны для этих данных: полуширина 0.381 pp при p=0.496 требует n≈66 161, 0.434 pp при p=0.61389 — n≈48 455, при фактических 276 строках (194 валидных). Числители нецелые: 0.496·194 = 96.22; 0.61389·194 = 119.09. Вывод: цитированные числа/CI — из другой единицы наблюдения или внешнего источника, не из этого CSV.

## Что осталось unknown (не выдаю за факты)
- **Неподтверждённое допущение**: что блок Q8 именно про *requirements*. В описании датасета буквально «Degree to which ML aspects are addressed by <role>» — слова «requirements» в файле нет; это интерпретация.
- `D4_Role='0'` (23 строки, из них 10 Completed) оставлен как NA, смысл кода — unknown.
- M2 self-attribution (только чувствительность): SA 75.0% (9/12), DS 74.576% (44/59), PL 62.5% (20/32), RE 0/2, Tester 0/2 — нерепрезентативно, в ответ не входит.
- Keyword-маппинг `D4_Role_Others` помечен как произвольный (DS 20, PL 11, Developer 6, BA 3, SA 2), в ответ не входит.
- 6 Suspended, ответивших на Q8, остались в базе; 21 респондент с нулём отмеченных ролей остались в знаменателе 194 (консервативно).

## Дисклеймер про 49.6% / 61.389% (без подгонки)
- Ничего не двигал: ни знаменатель, ни метрику, ни free-text. 49.6% аппроксимируется только Data Scientist (48.969% при n=194 / 49.468% при n=188); 61.389% не даёт ни одна роль ни при одной базе.

native_result.HypoB: Interviews are the most commonly used technique for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects: they rank first over Scenarios/Prototyping and Workshops/Meetings in every analysis base, with a recomputed prevalence of 50.0% of the 194 respondents who answered the Q9 block (bootstrap 95% CI [42.8%, 57.2%]; 55.7% among the 174 respondents naming at least one technique).
